note: Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 13:3b first colon +3 (the Ps 5:11a formula, copied as the glossary asks); 13:3c second colon −3; 13:6 −3 / +4 / +3 (the named subject ‘vós’ and ‘indigente’; the Latin colons are short). Rhyme flags: 13:5 Senhor / temor — a real accidental rhyme, sent to the critics; 13:7 Israel / Israel — the Latin’s own echo (Israël / Israël), rule 5’s exception.

Draft 1. Clean: no remark on any verse; the marks confirmed. Passed in particular ‘Corromperam-se’, ‘nos seus feitos’, ‘olhou do céu sobre’, ‘quem procure a Deus’, ‘Todos se desviaram’, the verbless ‘veneno de áspides debaixo dos seus lábios’ and ‘Ruína e infelicidade nos seus caminhos’, ‘Não hão de saber’, ‘vós envergonhastes’, ‘desviar o cativeiro’.

Draft 1. Four verses; best 13:3a, worst 13:7. «O salmo tem austeridade e força oral, sobretudo nas repetições e nas imagens corporais … os principais tropeços vêm de algumas construções calcadas no latim e do longo membro final.» All four taken — each changes only how the thing is said (D2).

outcomes.remark: «olhou sobre» soa transportada do latim → ‘Do céu, o Senhor olhou para os filhos dos homens’
outcomes.reason: The preposition taken (‘para’, Matos Soares 1932’s); his fronting of ‘Do céu’ not taken — the Latin’s order is good Portuguese. ‘sobre’ is option 2.

outcomes.remark: ‘velozes são os seus pés’: the inversion is declamatory → ‘os seus pés são velozes’
outcomes.reason: Order only (D2). Draft 1’s order is option 2.

outcomes.remark: ‘Senhor’ at the mediant rhymes with ‘temor’ at the end → ‘Ao Senhor não invocaram’
outcomes.reason: His line is the Latin’s own order (Dóminum non invocavérunt) and removes a rhyme the Latin does not have; the repetition timóre … timor untouched, as he asked.

outcomes.remark: «Desviar o cativeiro» soa pouco português; the long colon wants the direct order → ‘afastar o cativeiro … Jacó exultará e Israel se alegrará’
outcomes.reason: ‘afastar’ says avértere’s image in plain Portuguese (the glossary’s ‘desviar’ holds for a face or anger, not for a captivity); the direct order (decision exsultabit) is order only and ends the verse on the verb instead of a second ‘Israel’.

note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. 22 items, 4 unknown words (áspides, iniquidade, indigente, exultará). No wrong first hearing that the Latin excludes. Tests passed: ‘Todos se desviaram’ heard as turning from the good (not as parting); ‘vós envergonhastes’ heard as said to the evildoers (the Ps 10:2 remedy holds here); ‘Não hão de saber’ heard as ‘they will come to know’ — the Latin’s nonne. ‘desviar o cativeiro’ heard as ‘afastar ou evitar’, present or threatened — the Latin’s range, but the stylist’s verb was taken anyway. ‘indigente’ listed as unknown for the third time (Pss 11 ×2, 13).

outcomes.remark: plural subject after the singular ‘insensato’: the fools / mankind
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s plural (corrúpti sunt) after its singular (insípiens); left as open as the Latin.

outcomes.remark: ‘os filhos dos homens’: mankind (heard first) / male descendants
outcomes.reason: Glossary; heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘quem entenda’: understanding in general / understanding God (heard first)
outcomes.reason: intéllegens has no object in the Latin either.

outcomes.remark: ‘Todos se desviaram’: all people turned from the good (heard first) / the wicked just named
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; the test of ‘desviar-se’ against ‘apartar-se’ next to ‘juntos’ passed.

outcomes.remark: whose throat, tongues and lips: the wicked (heard first) / all mankind
outcomes.reason: eórum is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘sepulcro aberto’: rot / speech that kills
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s image, not explained.

outcomes.remark: ‘cheia de maldição e de amargura’: they utter curses (heard first) / they are cursed and bitter
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘Ruína e infelicidade nos seus caminhos’: they cause it (heard first) / they meet it
outcomes.reason: The Latin is open in the same way (in viis eórum).

outcomes.remark: ‘temor de Deus’: reverence (heard first) / fear of punishment
outcomes.reason: timor holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘Não hão de saber’: don’t they know? / they will come to know (heard first); no object
outcomes.reason: A question expecting ‘yes’ is heard as ‘they will know’: the Latin’s nonne cognóscent. No object in the Latin.

outcomes.remark: ‘o meu povo’: God speaking, unannounced (heard first) / the psalmist’s people
outcomes.reason: The Latin changes speaker the same way.

outcomes.remark: who did not invoke: the evildoers (heard first) / the people devoured
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘ali’: where they devoured / unnamed
outcomes.reason: illic is as unplaced.

outcomes.remark: ‘onde não havia temor’: no cause to fear (heard first) / no fear before / no reverence
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s repeated noun, open the same way.

outcomes.remark: ‘Porque …’ explains the trembling (heard first) or what follows
outcomes.reason: quóniam hangs the same way.

outcomes.remark: ‘na geração justa’: among the just / a just age (heard first)
outcomes.reason: generátio holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘vós envergonhastes’: the evildoers addressed (heard first) / the hearers
outcomes.reason: The test of the named subject passed: not heard as said to God.

outcomes.remark: ‘o conselho do indigente’: advice he gave (heard first) / his plan
outcomes.reason: consílium → conselho (glossary: open between advice and deliberation, as the Latin).

outcomes.remark: ‘a sua esperança’: the indigent’s (heard first) / the just generation’s
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘Quem dará de Sião’: who will bring salvation from Sion (heard first) / who in Sion will give
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘desviar o cativeiro’: end a present captivity / avert a threatened one (heard first: unclear)
outcomes.reason: The verb changed for the stylist’s sake (‘afastar’); the doubt present / threatened is the Latin’s own and stays.

outcomes.remark: ‘Jacó … Israel’: the people / a person and a country / one person
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s names, as they stand.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: áspides
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s snake named (rule 5); ‘cobras’ would lose the kind.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: iniquidade
outcomes.reason: Glossary (iníquitas → iniquidade).

outcomes.remark: unknown word: indigente
outcomes.reason: Kept under the glossary’s working rendering; the third ‘unknown’ is recorded in the row for the ruling.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: exultará
outcomes.reason: Glossary (exsultáre → exultar).

note: v2. Four verses changed against draft 1, all from the stylist and each order or construction only: 13:2 ‘olhou do céu para’ (was ‘sobre’); 13:3c ‘os seus pés são velozes’ (was ‘velozes são’); 13:5 ‘Ao Senhor não invocaram’ (the Latin’s order; removes the rhyme Senhor / temor); 13:7 ‘afastar o cativeiro’ (was ‘desviar’) and ‘Jacó exultará, e Israel se alegrará’ (was verb first). Nothing held against the Latinist (he had no remark). Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the three v1 critics read).
Draft 2: hard pass. Soft flags as draft 1 (13:3b +3, 13:3c −3, 13:6 −3 / +4 / +3); the two rhyme flags are gone (13:5 by the Latin’s order; 13:7 now ends on ‘alegrará’).
